title: THE EVERYDAY CITY
summary: A complete low-rise town organised around three living districts, a civic band and shared dry commons. An independent compute/repair campus and a new farm-learning edge support its southern approaches. Whole-site zoning and regional road studies frame conditional growth; housing, employment and resource figures are capacities to verify, not promised demand.

autonomy.human_role: Jingyuan Huang directed housing/public-life priorities, delegated node choices, requested English deliverables and directly authorised publication. After reviewing V2, he requested a fuller, less isolated farm-edge composition. Codex revised workshop siting, forecourts, rear servicing, cameras, diagrams and presentation; design content remains independently unassessed.

nodes_reason: A01 tests shared housing ground; B03 tests a separately serviced productive campus; C02 tests a new public/farm interface outside fixed pilots.

tradeoff.objective: Maximum uninterrupted compute throughput and minimum productive-route length
tradeoff.why: Independent housing, public life and a clear service boundary take precedence.
tradeoff.consequence: Flexible IT output, additional maintenance and walking connections, shared-space funding obligations.
tradeoff.who_bears: Compute investors and operators through interruption contracts; public-service funding must not depend on uninterrupted IT revenue.
